#125416. The Strongest Pre-Workout Powders to Fuel Your Training in 2025

📅 03 Mar 2025 • ⏱️ 24m • 📚 Deep Dive (4854 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Breakingmuscle ↗ Open Full Page

The Strongest Pre-Workout Powders to Fuel Your Training in 2025

📅 03 Mar 2025 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Breakingmuscle

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that whether you’re starting your fitness journey or you’re a weightlifting junkie, there are several supplements that should be staples in your stack.
  • Not far behind would be another supplement that can help you achieve your muscle-building and weight-loss goals: pre-workout.
  • However, just like not all barbells are created equal, neither are supps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that whether you’re starting your fitness journey or you’re a weightlifting junkie, there are several supplements that should be staples in your stack. As a certified personal trainer and nutrition coach, I’d put a high-quality whey protein powder and one of the best creatines at the top.

Not far behind would be another supplement that can help you achieve your muscle-building and weight-loss goals: pre-workout.

However, just like not all barbells are created equal, neither are supps. The strongest pre-workouts stand out from the pack because they are formulated with research-backed doses of four key ingredients — caffeine (at least 200 milligrams), L-citrulline (at least 4,000 milligrams), beta-alanine (at least 3,200 milligrams), and betaine (at least 2,500 milligrams) — for physical and mental performance enhancement.

To save you the trouble of sipping on something that won’t give you an effective muscle pump, our team of expert product testers tried more than 80 pre-workouts and reported which supplements delivered the most focus, power, and tingles. Then, with some guidance from a few other experts, our squad of CPTs, CNCs, CrossFit enthusiasts, and dedicated weightlifters narrowed down the list to the eight strongest pre-workouts so you can select the perfect match for your goals and preferences.

Medical disclaimer: This content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any newly introduced supplement or exercise regimen.

In a recent development, if your goal is to improve your athletic performance and power output in the gym, then we recommend Transparent Labs BULK BLACK. This supplement contains a potent combination of 4,000 milligrams of beta-alanine, 2,500 milligrams of betaine anhydrous, and 10 other active ingredients. Beta-alanine, a nonessential amino acid, may improve potential power output by reducing muscle fatigue, allowing you to push out a few more reps while you exercise. And studies show betaine anhydrous may improve muscular endurance. These ingredients work together to enhance your training, paving the way for strength gains over time.

Each serving of BULK BLACK also contains 350 milligrams of caffeine, which is close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Overall, the impressive formulation earns 4 out of 5 stars from our team, as we docked a point for the high caffeine content since it may be too intense for some people.

However, this high-stim pre-workout is certainly effective.

Recent findings suggest that cory Kessler, C.P.T., C.F.N.C., has tried more than 25 pre-workouts. He tested the Blue Raspberry flavor of BULK BLACK before a cardio workout, noting that he felt more energized and focused throughout his workout. “I started sweating almost immediately, and within five to 10 minutes, I had a boost of energy, a massive pump, and felt like I could lift harder and stronger,” he notes. Cory also experienced the tingling sensation common with high doses of beta-alanine.

Cory also enjoys using BULK BLACK before bodybuilding workouts since it contains 8,000 milligrams of citrulline malate. While more research is needed, some studies suggest citrulline malate may boost exercise and muscular performance.

Two other areas where BULK BLACK stands out: solubility and taste. Our team gave Transparent Labs perfect scores in both categories.

“BULK BLACK completely dissolved in my shaker bottle in only a few seconds with no clumps, grittiness, or residue,” Cory states.

Recent findings suggest that available in eight flavors ranging from Black Cherry to Watermelon Peach to Strawberry Mango, one of our other product testers chose the Blue Raspberry option, giving it 5 out of 5 stars for taste. However, there are some mixed reviews on Amazon about the taste, depending on which flavor you choose.

“It’s hard to describe the taste of Blue Raspberry, but that’s exactly what it tastes like. Not too sweet, which is a good thing,” he says.

Related: Transparent Labs BCAA Glutamine Review.

Legion Pulse is our pick for the strongest natural pre-workout because it’s free from artificial sweeteners, flavors, and colors and contains six active ingredients that support enhanced energy.

Sources indicate that as a CPT and CNC, I look for four main ingredients in a high-quality pre-workout supplement: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. Each plays a key role in enhancing athletic performance. Research reveals:.

In a recent development, legion Pulse contains all four, including 350 milligrams of caffeine per serving, which is very close to the recommended daily limit of 400 milligrams. Keep in mind that if you decide to try Pulse, it’s a good idea to monitor your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee or tea.

“To get the most out of pre-workout supplements without stomach issues, start with a lower dose to see how your body reacts,” says Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD. “Choose supplements with fewer stimulants if caffeine bothers you, or go for stimulant-free options.”.

Luckily, if you’re new to pre-workout or are caffeine-sensitive, you can also choose the non-stim version of Pulse. So, even though we’d like to see creatine in the formulation, we still give this a strong score of 4 out of 5 stars, especially since there’s a caffeine-free version.

One of our product testers has tried five different brands of pre-workout and puts Pulse atop her list because of its effectiveness.

It has been revealed that “I’ve been using Pulse three times a week for six months, and it always makes me feel energized and focused,” our tester says. “My goal is to improve my personal records and lift harder, so Pulse is my go-to when I train.”.

She reports that it typically takes 15 minutes for this high-stim pre-workout to kick in, and while it does give her tingles, it’s not overwhelming. “I never feel a drop-off, but rather a slow energy release,” she says.

Pulse comes in 22 flavors, including Pink Lemonade, Cherry Limeade, and Strawberry Kiwi, so there’s something to satisfy everyone’s taste buds. That noted, one of our testers gave Pulse 4 out of 5 stars for taste, noting that while it tastes sweet, there’s a “weird aftertaste.”.

Recent findings suggest that while the formulation and flavor options make this a top-rated pre-workout, Pulse is by no means a budget-friendly option. At around $45 for a 20-serving tub, it earns the lowest score of 1 out of 5 stars for price per serving.

While many strong pre-workouts cost around $2 per serving, Nutricost Pre-X is our pick for the strongest budget pre-workout because it costs less than half of that. At about $0.93 per serving, one tester called it “the best value on the market,” and I agree, giving this a perfect score of 5 out of 5 for price per serving.

Although some budget pre-workouts lack key ingredients, Pre-X contains the four main ones we like to see in a pre-workout: caffeine, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and L-citrulline. “The price is better than most other pre-workouts I’ve tried, especially for a supplement this good,” notes one tester.

Recent findings suggest that each serving of Pre-X has 300 milligrams of caffeine and 4,000 milligrams of L-citrulline, so you should feel energized and get a good pump with this pre-workout. “I got a decent pump and had a calm focus without feeling overstimulated,” one tester says.

Some testers say Pre-X has a slightly lower dosage of beta-alanine than some other pre-workouts on our list, but others say they experienced noticeable tingles during their workout.

Recent findings suggest that while testers did not experience any negative side effects when trying Pre-X, this pre-workout is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose. Some health experts have raised concerns about taking sucralose in high doses. As a CPT and someone who pays close attention to everything I put in my body, I tend to steer clear of artificial sweeteners. Because of this, we docked a point off the formulation score, giving Pre-X 4 out of 5 stars.

Industry observers note that nutricost Pre-X comes in five flavors, including Blue Raspberry, Peach Mango, and Watermelon. Collectively, our team gave this strong pre-workout 4.5 out of 5 stars for taste.

Recent findings suggest that “This tastes great ice cold or at room temperature. I look forward to drinking it before my workouts,” claims one tester who tried Blue Raspberry.

Another tester who tried Peach Mango also gave Pre-X his stamp of approval.

“No artificial sweetener taste at all. It has a nice flavor that’s not overly sweet.”.

Whether you like a strong pre-workout that’s sweet, sour, fruity, or tart, Jacked Factory NitroSurge has a fit for you. With 11 options, you can stick to your favorite or keep a few flavors in rotation to keep your taste buds on their proverbial toes. Between the deep lineup and satisfying flavors, NitroSurge earned a perfect score for taste.

One of our testers tried Strawberry Margarita, and let’s just say she was more than satisfied with her sipping experience.

“It’s wildly delicious. I’d drink this by the side of the pool over ice all day.”.

Sources indicate that another tester prefers Jacked Factory NitroSurge to some other strong pre-workouts he’s tried. “I did not like the Pink Lemonade flavor of Legion Pulse, but I would definitely use the Grape NitroSurge again,” he states.

Recent findings suggest that as for its effectiveness? For one of our product testers, it took about 20 minutes to feel NitroSurge kick in. At that point, he felt like he could lift harder.

“I usually work out in the morning because I feel most rested then, but even after taking this in the afternoon, I felt ‘jacked up’ and ready to go,” he states, adding that he experienced tingles and a slight drop off, but neither was overwhelming.

Another tester who regularly takes strong pre-workouts doubled the dosage. He remarked he got “a bit of a boost from it” but nothing like what you’ll get from other strong pre-workouts. Ultimately, this makes NitroSurge a solid choice for beginners, as you can see how you respond to a single serving before upping it to two scoops.

Besides the taste, I like that it’s budget-friendly while still including evidence-backed ingredients, like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, betaine anhydrous, caffeine anhydrous, L-theanine, theobromine, and AstraGin. AstraGin, also found in Transparent Labs BULK BLACK, is a plant-based compound formulated to enhance nutrient absorption. While AstraGin is safe at 0.5 milligrams per kilogram of body weight per day, more research is needed on the potential performance-enhancing benefits.

In a recent development, like some of the other pre-workouts on our list, NitroSurge is made with the artificial sweetener sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about taking in high doses. Also, Jacked Factory supplements do not undergo third-party testing, which ensures products include the ingredients listed on the label and nothing else. This is especially notable for athletes who undergo drug testing for banned substances. We only gave Nitrosurge 3 out of 5 stars in this category since it is made in a Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP)-certified and FDA-registered facility.

For bodybuilders, a “pump” is a sign of a successful training session. Increased blood flow to the muscles makes them feel fuller and appear larger and more vascular during and after a workout. A pump also promotes muscle growth by delivering essential nutrients and oxygen to the muscles as blood flow increases. While you can achieve a pump through high-rep sets, drop sets, and supersets, high-stim pre-workouts like Gorilla Mode are specially designed to improve your pump.

Gorilla Mode contains several pump-enhancing ingredients in each scoop, including 5,000 milligrams of pure L-citrulline (more per scoop than any other pre-workout on our list) and 2,000 milligrams of Hydro Prime glycerol powder. L-citrulline works to widen blood vessels, increasing blood flow to the muscles. Glycerol powder is rapidly absorbed by the muscles and draws in water, which can cause muscle cell swelling.

If you’re caffeine-sensitive or budget-conscious, this intense pre-workout may not be the best for you. Although one serving only contains 200 milligrams of caffeine, you will need to take two servings to get research-backed doses of some key ingredients, including creatine monohydrate (only 2.5 gram per serving). At that point, you’d be at 400 milligrams of caffeine, which is the total amount the FDA says is safe for adults to consume per day. For this reason, we docked a point off the formulation, giving Gorilla Mode 4 out of 5 stars in this category.

Don’t forget that this also impacts how much bang you get for your buck. A 40-serving tub costs $60, and you’ll end up going through it that much quicker if you take two scoops before your training sessions. That would bring the cost to $3 per serving. So, from a value standpoint, we can only give Gorilla Mode 2.5 out of 5 stars.

On the other hand, this pricey supplement earned a strong score of 4.5 out of 5 stars for its effectiveness. One of our testers uses strong pre-workouts several times a week and tried Gorilla Mode before an upper-body workout. “Not only did I have a good pump, I also felt more focused. I knocked out a few more reps than usual during my workout,” he claims. “I like the Fruit Punch flavor, although it was sweeter than I thought it would be.”.

Industry observers note that while our tester enjoyed Gorilla Mode’s taste, he indicates the powder was gritty and difficult to mix properly. This is likely due to the glycerol powder, which absorbs moisture, leading to clumping.

If you like feeling skin tingles after taking your pre-workout, check out Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train. I love the prickly skin sensation because it lets me know my pre-workout is kicking in and it’s time to train. This temporary side effect, called paresthesia, is caused by beta-alanine, which works to increase muscular endurance.

Intensive Pre-Train has 3,500 milligrams of beta-alanine per serving, which is more per serving than almost all of the other pre-workouts on our list. “Beta-alanine is found in most pre-workout supplements, likely because it helps reduce fatigue and improve endurance in the short term,” states registered dietitian Alex Oskian. “This is because it reduces acidity in the body, which comes from lactic acid build-up.”.

In a recent development, our product tester used Crazy Nutrition Intensive Pre-Train before a high-intensity interval training (HIIT) workout and felt the tingles within 15 minutes. “These were strong compared to some other pre-workouts I’ve tried,” he notes. “I felt good tingles in my hands and face, which lasted for about an hour.”.

Earning a 5 out of 5 for effectiveness, Intense Pre-Train is also available in a caffeine-free version for those who don’t want stimulants in their pre-workout. The non-stim version comes in Green Apple, which our tester says tasted more like a greens powder than a sour apple.

“I’m rather caffeine-dependent, so I didn’t feel a burst of energy. I prefer caffeinated pre-workouts, but this is a great option for a late-night lifting session,” she says. Other testers who tried the Fruit Punch flavor say they enjoyed the tangy taste. To enhance the flavor, Crazy Nutrition is sweetened with the artificial sweetener sucralose. With some mixed reviews on the different flavors, we give this pre-workout a 3.5 out of 5 for taste.

Recent findings suggest that onnit Alpha Brain is designed to increase mental acuity and focus. Testers say that’s exactly how they felt after trying Onnit Alpha Brain, which is why it’s our pick for the strongest pre-workout for focus.“What makes this pre-workout stand out is the cognitive effects. I felt significantly more focused after taking Alpha Brain than any other pre-workout I’ve tried,” says one of our testers.

Other testers agreed, saying Alpha Brain helped them feel present and ready to work out without being overstimulated, leading to an effectiveness score of 4 out of 5 stars.

In a recent development, onnit Alpha Brain’s formula differs from most other strong pre-workout supplements on our list — it contains nootropics, substances that enhance learning and memory. One of the key ingredients, NooGandha, is an ashwagandha extract that can reduce stress and enhance well-being by reducing cortisol levels in the body.

Industry observers note that another key ingredient, AlphaSize, may promote the production of acetylcholine, a powerful neurotransmitter that enhances cognitive function. However, studies demonstrating the effect of alpha-GPC on cognitive performance used 200 to 400 milligram doses per day, and a serving of Onnit Alpha brain has 125 milligrams.

The other unique ingredient in Onnit Alpha Brain is Dynamine. It works similarly to caffeine, by blocking the body’s adenosine receptors that cause you to feel tired. However, this ingredient is banned in all sports supplements in Australia. While Dynamine is still allowed for sports competitions in the U.S., it is possible it will be banned in the future. Competitive athletes may want to steer clear of this product.

One of our testers notes Alpha Brain is only middle-of-the-road compared to other strong pre-workouts when it comes to physical energy. “After taking other strong pre-workouts, I usually experience a boost in energy. After taking this pre-workout, the mental effects were much more noticeable than the physical ones,” she says. That may be in part because Alpha Brain lacks ingredients like betaine anhydrous, taurine, and creatine, which can support muscle growth and recovery.

Industry observers note that we give the formulation 4 out of 5 stars thanks to the inclusion of nootropics, which are rapidly becoming more prevalent in the supplement market. But be aware that this probably isn’t your best bet for boosting your physical energy levels.

In a recent development, long before the days of gummy and ready-to-drink (RTD) pre-workout options, the most popular choice was the original C4. The latest version, C4 Ultimate, is more concentrated than the classic formula, combining both exercise performance and cognitive-enhancing ingredients.

One of our testers tried C4 Ultimate before a 30-minute HIIT workout, reporting that the caffeine blend got her zoned in before her training.

“I felt great throughout the entire workout,” she reported, giving C4 Ultimate a perfect score for effectiveness.

Sources indicate that this high-stim pre-workout is sweetened with sucralose, which some health experts have raised concerns about. While our tester doesn’t mind a very sweet pre-workout, the Icy Blue Razz flavor was a little too sugary for her liking. Mixing it in more water than recommended balances out the sweetness.

However, another tester was blown away by the Sour Batch Bros flavor, saying it tasted “just like Sour Patch Kids.” Taking both of their experiences into consideration, we’ll meet in the middle and give C4 Ultimate a 4 out of 5 for taste, especially since it comes in multiple flavors.

In a recent development, another plus for this product: It contains creatine — a popular supplement among athletes and bodybuilders for its ability to boost strength, enhance recovery, and prevent injury. Because of its performance-enhancing capabilities, some people like to take creatine in addition to their pre-workout. If you want the best of both worlds, we recommend C4 Ultimate.

Industry observers note that keep in mind that one serving contains 1.5 grams of creatine per serving, which is less than the recommended value of 3 to 5 grams daily. If you want to get the most performance-enhancing benefits from creatine, you should invest in a standalone supplement to help support your fitness goals.One final note: If you compete in a sport that requires drug testing, C4 Ultimate may not be the best strong pre-workout for you because it’s made with Dynamine, which is presently banned for use in Australia.

Our team of expert testers includes certified personal trainers, nutrition coaches, and CrossFit enthusiasts. As dedicated lifters and lovers of all things health and fitness, we’ve collectively tried more than 80 pre-workouts, giving us a broad perspective of what’s available on the market.

We tested each supplement before a workout, and in some cases, for several weeks or months, to evaluate its performance-enhancing benefits, taste, and whether the supplement had any negative side effects.

Using a 1-5 scoring system, we rated each pre-workout on a variety of factors, including:.

At the end of the testing period, we compared feedback to whittle our list down to only the best of the best. We also received valuable input from nutrition experts on what makes a strong pre-workout.

A strong pre-workout contains a combination of performance-enhancing ingredients in research-backed dosages. “Usually, the strength of a pre-workout is based upon the amount of stimulants it contains. High doses of caffeine (300+ milligrams) are usually a quick identifier of the pre-workout’s strength,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says.

It has been revealed that however, the potency of a pre-workout goes beyond the caffeine content. Other active ingredients like L-citrulline, beta-alanine, and betaine anhydrous can impact energy, focus muscular endurance, and power output.

“Stronger via the amount of caffeine isn’t always better. If the goal is a bigger pump in the gym, other ingredients like L-citrulline may be better,” states Alex. “Another common ingredient that can help a pre-workout feel stronger is beta-alanine, which may cause a tingling or ‘pins and needles’ sensation on the skin.”.

According to recent reports, it’s also important to remember that “strong” is a subjective term. For example, I can handle a full scoop of RedCon1 Total War without a problem, but I have friends who get too many tingles from a single serving.

Industry observers note that “Everyone’s body reacts differently to various compounds, so what works for one person might not be best for another,” indicates Dr. Christopher Mohr, Ph.D., RD.

A strong, well-dosed pre-workout supplement may help you train harder by boosting your energy, focus, and endurance during intense workouts.

“There are a few things that are really helpful when you are looking for a great gym session: energy to do the work, mental clarity to help focus on what you are doing (not just to work the muscle, but to prevent injury), and a great workout,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says. “Using a pre-workout may just help you achieve all of these.”.

Let’s explore the potential benefits of taking a strong pre-workout before you start your training session.

Caffeine is one of the most popular stimulants used in pre-workout supplements to enhance energy levels and improve focus. Almost all of the pre-workouts on our list use caffeine and L-theanine. Studies have shown when paired with caffeine, L-theanine may improve cognitive performance.

“Most pre-workouts contain the stimulant caffeine in higher dosages. L-theanine helps counteract the unwanted effects of caffeine supplementation: jittery feelings and a post-caffeine crash,” Alex indicates. “You might see less mental fatigue, improved reaction time, and fewer headaches while regularly supplementing with L-theanine.”.

I like taking a pre-workout to improve my focus because it helps intensify my workout and keep me #lockedin. Several pre-workouts on our list contain Alpha-GPC and tyrosine to give you that zoned-in feeling. Research suggests Alpha-GPC may improve cognitive function, and tyrosine may increase dopamine levels and cognition. One study found L-tyrosine helped improve people’s memory while they worked on a demanding task.

Recent findings suggest that A pre-workout may help you squeeze out a few more reps as you work to build strength and muscle. Two ingredients commonly used in pre-workout, beta-alanine and betaine anhydrous, may help reduce fatigue and support muscular endurance.

In a recent development, “Research suggests betaine anhydrous can improve muscle strength and power via increased total work capacity and improved protein synthesis within the body. Simply put, you can do more work, which leads to increased strength and muscle growth,” says Alex.

Another common ingredient, taurine, may improve your performance and power.

Sources indicate that registered dietitian Alex Oskian says not every pre-workout is created equal, so it’s vital to pay attention to what’s on the label. “Supplements are not regulated by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This means the supplement might not contain all the ingredients you’re looking for and may even contain unwanted ingredients,” she says. Alex recommends looking for supplements that undergo third-party testing.

Sources indicate that if you choose a high-stim pre-workout, be mindful of your caffeine intake from other sources like coffee, tea, or soda so that you don’t go over the daily recommended value of 400 milligrams. This will help prevent potential negative side effects like jitters, anxiety, or trouble falling asleep.

“Consuming caffeine at the end of your day may cause sleep disturbances, which only hurts performance in the long run,” indicates Oskian.

No matter which pre-workout you choose, it’s crucial to follow the recommended intake guidelines. Remember, pre-workouts should not be taken more than once per day.

Industry observers note that “Pre-workout supplements are generally safe for healthy adults, but they can have some potential side effects,” states Dr. Raj Dasgupta, MD, FACP, FCCP, FAASM. “It is vital to start with a low dose and talk to your doctor before taking them, especially if you have any underlying health conditions.”.

There are a number of crucial factors to consider when deciding which strong pre-workout is right for you, including:.

Many strong pre-workouts incorporate a variety of active ingredients. When choosing a pre-workout supplement, consider your goals. For example, a bodybuilder may prefer a pre-workout powder that’s highly caffeinated and contains ingredients such as L-citrulline, betaine anhydrous, and creatine to help improve performance. On the other hand, an endurance athlete may want a pre-workout that has less caffeine but includes beta-alanine, BCAAs, and mineral electrolytes.

It has been revealed that whenever possible, I choose supplements that are tested by a third party for purity and have transparent labeling. Athletes who undergo drug testing should look for certifications from Informed Choice and NSF, which ensure the product does not include any banned substances.

According to recent reports, although we test all of the products we recommend, it’s important to check out customer reviews, especially from people with similar fitness goals and preferences. They can provide valuable insights into the product’s overall effectiveness, potential side effects, and the most popular flavors.

In a recent development, “Recommended brands and products are ones that are highly rated by owners and contain ingredients that have been backed by scientific research,” notes Dr. Raj Dasgupta.

According to recent reports, “Taste plays a big role in pre-workout selection. If you don’t like a particular flavor, then you likely won’t drink the pre-workout no matter its benefits,” Oskian says. It’s also important to consider the use of artificial flavors, colors, and sweeteners.

In a recent development, the price of a pre-workout doesn’t necessarily reflect its effectiveness. Understanding the ingredients list and dosage levels is crucial to ensure you’re paying for a high-quality supplement and not just expensive marketing.

There are a few potential red flags you want to avoid when picking out a pre-workout.

I like to avoid supplements made using proprietary blends. These blends are combinations of ingredients, but the individual doses are not fully disclosed. This lack of transparency makes it impossible to assess the effectiveness and safety of the supplement.

Many fitness enthusiasts and athletes prefer all-natural ingredients and products free from unnecessary fillers or additives. “If sugar alcohols and artificial sweeteners wreak havoc on your stomach, make sure those aren’t on the ingredient list,” registered dietitian Alex Oskian says.

Athletes who compete in sanctioned organizations should make sure the supplements they use are third-party tested and certified banned substance-free.

If you have substantial fitness goals, choosing a strong pre-workout formulated with safe and effective doses of science-backed ingredients is worth it to deliver performance-enhancing effects. Keep in mind that even the strongest pre-workouts on the market won’t make you run faster, lift heavier, or exercise longer on their own. These supplements are designed to help you put in the work at the gym to make gains and enhance your performance over time.

Ultimately, though, a strong pre-workout is only part of the equation to becoming the strongest version of yourself. At the end of the day, you have to put in the work, follow a sound nutrition proposal, and prioritize rest and recovery to crush your fat-burning and muscle-building goals.

Yes, technically, you can take a pre-workout made with 400 milligrams of caffeine. However, that is the maximum daily dose recommended by the FDA. This means if you’re using a high-stim pre-workout, you may want to avoid caffeine from other sources like coffee, tea, soda, or energy drinks. Since 400 milligrams is the maximum recommended daily dose, I do not advise using a pre-workout containing 600 milligrams of caffeine.

A pre-workout can directly and indirectly make you stronger. A well-dosed pre-workout may help you add a few pounds to your lifts or allow you to push out a few more reps during your workout. However, real strength gains will come from consistent training, proper nutrition, and recovery. If a pre-workout supplement helps you stay consistent in the gym, it may also help you gain strength and muscle mass.

Yes. Depending on your sensitivity to stimulants like caffeine, you may experience side effects, including jitters, anxiety, or difficulty falling asleep. If this is the case, use a half serving or a more moderately dosed pre-workout to assess your tolerance.

Six Dumb Misconceptions About The Economy (that the Politicians Want You To Believe)

📅 13 Oct 2024 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2016 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Well, it looks like we’re here in another US election year already.
  • Industry observers note that as Advanced Mustachians, we already know that the ongoing battle of Harris vs.
  • But out of all the things the politicians like to bicker about, there’s one area where MMM does need to set the record straight, and that area is of course money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Well, it looks like we’re here in another US election year already.

Industry observers note that as Advanced Mustachians, we already know that the ongoing battle of Harris vs. Trump should not be consuming much of our time. Sure, we do our research and cast our votes but after that we move right on to focus on other things within our own circle of control.

But out of all the things the politicians like to bicker about, there’s one area where MMM does need to set the record straight, and that area is of course money. Your money, the economy in general, and the overall wealth of the nation.

Recent findings suggest that politicians are already not known for being the sharpest tools in the shed when it comes to technical stuff like science, technology, or economics. But this year the discourse has become particularly dumb, as our candidates try to manipulate undecided voters in swing states with ideas that are based on irrational emotions rather than sound economic sense.

For one particularly funny example, you may have noticed that the competing party (Trump in this case) is attacking the incumbents (Biden/Harris) over the “bad economy.” When in fact the US economy is stronger than it has ever been, with the lowest unemployment we’ve ever seen as well.

It’s hard to imagine a better situation than we have right now, and in fact the recent bout of higher inflation is a sign that things have been going too well, and we needed to step on the brakes with the help of higher interest rates.

But somehow the people still seem to believe that we have a “bad” economy. Take a look at this Gallup poll showing that while most people (85%) are doing really well right now, they assume that it’s just their own good fortune – only 17% believe the economy is doing well.

According to recent reports, this is mathematically impossible, because if most people are doing well, that’s the definition of a good economy! And suspiciously enough, this widespread wrongness correlates quite nicely with the rise of social media misinformation.

So the politicians and the news have been doing the opposite of what they should be doing in an ideal situation (sharing accurate information). And sure, we can always just ignore their speeches and go on with our lives. But when it comes to economics, knowledge is power (and money). The more accurately we understand how things really work, the wealthier we will all become.

So with all that in mind, I hereby present you with my list of the….

Top Dumb Things Politicians Want You To Believe About The Economy.

1: The President Controls the Economy.

In a recent development, if there’s a recession, the opposition party likes to blame it on the current president. If the economy is booming, the current president likes to give himself (or possibly soon herself) credit for all of that success. But really, the US economy is way too major – and thankfully way too free – for the president to control or really even influence all that strongly.

Recent findings suggest that in reality, our economy is a gigantic machine which converts labor and materials into things like iPhones, hospitals and pumpkin pies. And although we’re the biggest economy at 26% of the planet, we are still heavily influenced by that much bigger 74% of economic activity that the other 7.6 billion people on Earth are busy producing everywhere else.

When we have our inevitable little boom and bust cycles, they are mostly caused by the normal cycle of irrational exuberance (and greed) like the 2007 housing boom, followed by brief periods of extreme fear and pessimism like the 2008-2012 financial and housing crash.

Recent findings suggest that the government does play a role too, by setting tax rates and other rules. But the effects of these policies are usually so delayed and unpredictable, that you can’t draw a straight line between today’s president and today’s economy. In other words, the government does its best to adjust the rudder on our giant ship, but in the short term our economy lurches around on the waves and storms of the ocean.

2: The President Controls Interest Rates.

Industry observers note that this one is especially funny to me, as our candidates feign sympathy for the hard life of middle class Americans, who now face higher borrowing costs on their credit cards and car loans and mortgages. They claim they will fight to bring the interest rates down. Trump even goes as far as bullying our Federal Reserve board members (who can only do their jobs if we allow them to function as independent experts) and suggesting that he would take over the whole department, if elected.

In a recent development, the real story is that while monetary policy would be a terrible tool to leave in the hands of a sitting president (see Argentina), it does function as an excellent set of gas and brake pedals for the economy if used properly. When things slow down and unemployment gets too high, a cut to the interest rates will produce a boost in everything from new jobs to stock prices. But if things get too hot, you get rapid inflation which can mess up the system.

3: Inflation has Made Life Harder for Americans (and the President Can Magically Reverse it).

This line of reasoning is even dumber than the last one. For a couple of years after the Covid era, we had rapid inflation. It was caused by a rare combination of a goods shortage caused by things like factory closures and remote work, plentiful demand from government stimulus spending and low interest rates. These factors have since ironed themselves out, and inflation is back down to an ultra-low 2.4%.

But most significantly, wages have still risen faster than inflation so we are all better off than before! Since 2019, overall prices are up 19% and our wages are up 21%. So even after all that inflation, we are still doing just fine. But the candidates are still bickering over inflation as if it’s an actual problem, and even worse promising to “bring prices back down”. And they’ve managed to convince the electorate that “higher wages and prices” is the same thing as “a bad economy”. Which is just plain wrong.

In a recent development, bonus dumbness: politicians also occasionally blame “greedy corporations” for increasing prices to hoard profits. While price increases are totally acceptable in a market system (as a business owner you are free to set prices wherever you like), in reality it doesn’t usually happen because our markets are too competitive. For example, a recent deep analysis from NPR showed that no, grocery stores haven’t made any windfall profit at all off of this recent bout of Covid-fueled inflation.

4: The President Controls Housing Prices.

One important thing that has changed over the past ten years is that US house prices and rents have both risen much faster than general inflation and even wages. On the positive side, interest rates have also risen which tends to make houses feel more expensive and is supposed to help bring house prices down. But it hasn’t happened yet which means we have the double whammy of higher prices and higher interest costs for mortgage borrowers.

Sources indicate that the dumb part is that our candidates are proposing things that would make the problem even worse, like subsidies for first-time homebuyers or schemes to reduce the interest rates. When really the solution is to increase the supply of housing, which I personally think will happen if we stop putting up roadblocks for homebuilders (myself included) to build housing.

Things like faster and cheaper permits, less onerous and expensive building codes, eliminating suburban-style zoning and setback and car parking rules, and changing laws so that NIMBYs no longer get any say over what other people do with their own land could all help reduce the cost of building a house by about 50%, rapidly and permanently.

5: The President Controls Gas Prices, and They Are At the moment “High” and We Want Them Lower.

Industry observers note that ahh, gasoline! The most ridiculous of things to worry about and the fuel for many of MMM’s rants since 2011.

First of all, on an inflation-adjusted basis, gasoline is still about the same price as it was in 1950: in the $3-4 range per gallon, in today’s dollars.

According to recent reports, secondly, it is so cheap that even with our huge inefficient American vehicles, the average household is still only spending 2.5% of their disposable income on the stuff! (The funny part is that they spend many times more on the rest of the car ownership experience while thinking gas is the part that is expensive).

Third, gasoline has been obsolete for almost a decade now. You can get a used electric car for less than the price of a comparable used gas car, or if you’re a fancypants money waster like me, fresh EVs are also cheaper than their gas counterparts. You get a faster, nicer car that almost never needs maintenance OR gasoline, and save money.

In a recent development, so why are we even still talking about this antique fuel of a previous era? Why aren’t the candidates also arguing over the price of Kodak film or typewriters or fax machines?

6: The Economy is Something We Should Even Worry About.

The funniest part about all this economic talk is that we’re focusing on the wrong thing. While hard work and business and advancing the frontiers of human knowledge are all fun things, the reality is that we passed the point of having “Enough” decades ago. When the American middle class complains about how hard we have it these days, it’s like a bunch of overfed people at a buffet wishing they could just have one more flavor of donuts stacked onto the table.

Recent findings suggest that yes, we have income and wealth inequality so that the rich tend to get richer more rapidly. And yes, we should keep that in check with a somewhat progressive tax system because a more equal society tends to be a more peaceful and happy one.

It has been revealed that but have you noticed that as the rich people get richer, they don’t get any happier? It’s because after you pass the point of “Enough”, adding more money doesn’t really help much.

Recent findings suggest that and “Enough” is much more defined by your mindset (and your collection of life skills) than your paycheck. So if the politicians really cared about improving our happiness and wellbeing, they’d be preaching the Principles of Mustachianism rather than pandering to the specific requests of coal miners or billionaires.

But alas, winning an election is a very different thing than proposing stuff that is actually best for the country. And for that reason, we cast our votes for the best party and then tune back out until the next election.

In the Comments: Has the election season been getting you down, pumping you up, or just giving you a thorough dose of “Meh”?

It has been revealed that while researching economic stats for this article, I came across a quirky but informative series of videos called USA Facts by none other than former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer. It seems that he had the same frustration as me: Americans are fighting over a bunch of opinions and misinformation without even bothering to look up the actual facts. So he made a well-produced series of videos that just share the facts without the baggage of political hype on top of them. I wish our politicians could do the same thing!

The Best Smith Machine for Your Home Gym in 2025

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Other than the almighty treadmill, there may not be a piece of equipment more synonymous with commercial gyms than the Smith machine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Other than the almighty treadmill, there may not be a piece of equipment more synonymous with commercial gyms than the Smith machine. Boasting tremendous versatility and functionality, this muscle-building tool is popular among lifters of all experience levels.

In a recent development, however, you don’t need a gym membership to enjoy its benefits. While it may have not been a home gym staple years ago, the Smith machine has become a must-have for many fitness enthusiasts. Offering added protection without a spotter for your bench presses, back squats, deadlifts, and other strength exercises, the Smith machine is a wise investment for those trying to build the ultimate garage gym.

It has been revealed that with options spanning from traditional Smith machines to all-in-one home gym solutions, you might feel a bit overwhelmed about which direction to go. Luckily for you, our team of expert product testers did all the due diligence necessary to separate the cream from the crop. From analyzing the build materials to testing the smoothness of the bar path to assessing the value, we took the time to dissect each element in order to narrow down our list to just five.

It has been revealed that in addition, we got some valuable insight from Mauro S. Maietta, district fitness and education manager for Crunch Fitness, on the benefits and what factors to consider when you’re shopping for a Smith machine.

It has been revealed that this content is meant to be informative, but should not be taken as medical advice. It is not intended for use as diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of health problems. Always speak with your doctor before starting any new supplement or exercise regimen.

Industry observers note that if you’re searching for a multifunctional Smith machine that’s compatible with a ton of attachments, the Force USA G15 is the machine that can truly do it all — albeit at an expensive price point of around $5,500. However, there’s a reason it earned 4.5 out of 5 stars for versatility from our top product tester: you can perform a wide variety of exercises by taking advantage of all of its functionality.

According to recent reports, tipping the scales at nearly 1,000 pounds, the G15 combines a functional trainer, half rack, and Smith machine into a single, sturdy unit. Measuring over 6 feet wide, over 4 feet deep, and about 7 feet tall, the G15 earns a 4-star footprint rating. While there are more compact options, it’s still a good option for folks with limited space, especially considering the versatility you get.

Offering dual 289-pound weight stacks that keep it well-anchored, the G15 also scores 4 out of 5 stars for durability and construction.

“This thing is like a tank,” our tester says. “Once it’s assembled, it’ll basically be stuck in place.”.

Unfortunately, our tester wasn’t as impressed with the cable pulley material. Asthey’re made from nylon instead of aluminum, they don’t move as smoothly and won’t be as durable as their metal counterparts.

Sources indicate that something that separates the G15 from many competitors is its ability to go from a 2:1 or 4:1 pulley ratio. This gives you the ability to make the weight feel like half or a quarter of the actual weight. While our tester would prefer a 1:1 ratio for more effective resistance, he says the 2:1 or 4:1 ratios “will be adequate for most people working out from home.”.

Recent findings suggest that the G15 comes with a lengthy list of attachments, including J-hooks, safety spotter arms, multi-grip dip handles, a multi-grip pull-up bar, band pegs, and a low row footplate. If you want to unlock even more training possibilities, the $700 G15 Upgrade Kit includes three additional strength training stations, three functional attachments, a TV mount, and four storage shelves.

Two knocks against this ultra-versatile machine: assembly and value.

Although some of the parts arrive pre-assembled, our assembly expert recommends budgeting “at least 20 man hours” to get the G15 fully put together. And if you want to leave it to the professionals, you’ll need to pay an additional $800.

At nearly $6,000 on its own, the G15 certainly isn’t made for budget-conscious shoppers. Our top product tester gave it 3.5 out of 5 stars for value, noting that Force USA could use better quality components, cables, and accessories, including one of the key parts of this premium-priced unit: the built-in barbell.“The knurling is super passive and not going to allow for an adequate grip for the user if you were to go heavy on any Smith machine movements,” he explains.

Want to crush a full-body workout with a single piece of equipment? The Titan Fitness Smith Machine can be the all-in-one solution that allows you to train your upper body, lower body, and core in a safe, effective manner.

Recent findings suggest that is it as versatile as the G15? No. Is it far more affordable? Yes.

Sources indicate that for less than a third of the price, you can still get an excellent workout experience from the $1,7000 Titan Smith Machine. One of our more seasoned product testers used it for a variety of strength training sessions, highlighting how impressed she was by the smooth glide of the barbell and the angled design. In addition, this Smith machine is counterbalanced so you don’t have to support the entire 45-pound barbell like you do on other machines. Beginners will appreciate this, as the bar only feels like 15 pounds.

Unfortunately, like Force USA, Titan left our team wanting more out of the knurling.

“It’s fine for a Smith machine, but it’s definitely not the most grippy bar,” our tester notes.

Sources indicate that on the other hand, this machine earns high marks for its ergonomics. Our tester rated it 4 out of 5 stars in this category. She found the single-axis, angled design helped improve her muscle activation during lower-body weight training exercises like Smith machine squats and lunges.

Sources indicate that most importantly, she felt completely secure using this Titan machine. Not only was there no wobbling or shaking, but the bar moved smoothly, leading her to give a 5-out-of-5 rating for stability.

Sources indicate that “This is a super stable machine; there was no give to it even when we were using heavy weights,” our tester says. “This was ultra-smooth.” While Titan priced this machine fairly, we’d like to see a better warranty. A one-year policy falls well short of what we expect from most brands. Plus, if you want to return a piece of equipment, you must pay the return shipping costs and a 20% restocking fee. That results in a disappointing customer experience score of just 2 out of 5 stars.

Recent findings suggest that don’t want a standalone Smith machine? Bolt Fitness has a space-saving solution in the form of the Storm Series Stinger Smith Machine Attachment. Compatible with any 3” x 3” frame using 1” hardware, this universal attachment can seamlessly integrate with your existing squat or power rack, opening the door to even more training possibilities.

We rate this Smith machine attachment a 4.5 out of 5 for versatility, as it offers 12 different positions totaling 60” of vertical adjustments. That means you can quickly go from a steep incline bench press to a Romanian deadlift, making your workouts more efficient, too. Plus, we also like that this attachment has a 43” built-in multi-grip pull-up bar, giving you the ability to develop your vertical pulling strength and endurance.

Industry observers note that bolt also earns solid marks for construction, earning 4 out of 5 stars in this key category. However, our chief product tester warns not to expect quite the same level of craftsmanship as some better-known brands.

“You won’t see the same quality welds or powder coats from Bolt as you will from Rogue or REP,” he indicates.

Like several other nominees on this list, our tester was also disappointed with the Smith bar’s knurling. The passive knurl pattern won’t give you a particularly stable grip, especially when using heavier weights.

“You definitely won’t mistake this for an Olympic barbell,” our tester claims.

As for the price? At around $1,100 this is on the expensive side for a Smith machine attachment. For example, the Bells of Steel Smith Machine Rack Attachment is much more affordable at $800. We rate it a 3 out of 5 for value, especially since you already need a rack to use it. Otherwise, expect to invest a significant chunk of change to get a fully functioning setup.

Just because you can’t afford to splurge on something like the G15 doesn’t mean you can’t find a Smith machine that fits within your budget. If you don’t have a ton of financial wiggle room, the RitFit Smith Machine is the most affordable option that earned our stamp of approval.

As our top product tester puts it, “If you’re looking for a Smith machine and you’re on an ultra-budget, this is it.”.

At about $500 on Amazon, this machine is less than a third of the price of the Titan Fitness Smith Machine and less than a tenth of the cost of the G15. Of course, it’s not the most durable option on the market, but it offers sufficient versatility at a very attractive price point to earn a near-perfect value rating of 4.5 out of 5 stars.

Dubbed the “sleeper pick” by our tester, he notes that “the low price covers so many sins.”.

Before we dive into some of RitFit’s shortcomings, let’s highlight some of the strengths of this machine. First, we rated it 4 out of 5 for versatility, as it offers built-in low row and lat pulldown capabilities using a plate-loaded cable pulley system that holds 165 pounds. The RitFit Smith Machine also comes with several attachments, including a pin-on landmine row and two multi-purpose pull-up handles.

Secondly, it has a compact design that makes it suitable for home gym setups with limited  space. It also weighs just 140 pounds, making it easier to move than other options on this list.

However, our tester had several callouts about the RitFit Smith Machine that deserve mentioning. With cheaper build materials and a lightweight design, it didn’t prove to be as stable as he would have liked, earning just 3.5 out of 5 stars for both construction and stability. Needless to say, this isn’t the best option if you want to lift heavy weights. Still, considering you could pay around the same price for a high-quality Olympic barbell, the RitFit Smith Machine is a solid option if you’re on a limited budget.

Imagine if you could turn your squat rack into a Smith machine in a matter of minutes. That dream can be a reality if you’re willing to invest around $700 on the VTS Lite Rack Attachment from Bulletproof Fitness, a lesser-known fitness equipment manufacturer that’s caught our attention.

Recent findings suggest that while we haven’t gotten our hands on this attachment just yet, it’s hard not to get excited about the concept and execution by Bulletproof. The Versa Trolley System (VTS) Lite allows you to convert your squat rack into a Smith machine using your own barbell. The rollers are made from UHMW plastic, an ultra-durable material we’ve seen used on other racks. This attachment only weighs 15 pounds, making the VHS Lite a more user-friendly alternative than the full-sized VTS, which weighs in at 24 pounds. From a construction standpoint, we feel comfortable giving the VTS Lite 4 out of 5 stars.

It has been revealed that in addition, we like that Bulletproof offers a wide range of options to accommodate different racks. You can choose between a 3” x 3” pair, a 2” x 3” pair, or a 2” x 2” pair. You also can choose different hook sizes based on the diameter of your barbell. This optionality, along with the added exercise variety you get from using the attachments, earns a 4.5 out of 5 for versatility.

Set to be released in May 2025, we’re excited to see this product in action. If you want a more streamlined solution than getting a standalone Smith machine, this is an attractive space- and money-saving solution. Based on the price and versatility, we give it a value rating of 4 out of 5 — though it could go higher once we get our hands on it.

As Smith machines have become more popular among the home gym community, we’ve ramped up our efforts to test ones from a variety of brands. This has allowed us to develop a thorough evaluation process that examines a number of key factors that impact your workout experience.

With options ranging from standard Smith machines to all-in-one trainers with cable machines, here’s what we assess during testing using a 1-5 scoring system:.

Industry observers note that what makes a Smith machine such a valuable training tool? If you’ve ever used one, you already know there’s added peace of mind knowing you have built-in support. Here’s an overview of the different benefits of utilizing this popular piece of equipment.

Recent findings suggest that unlike when you use a barbell and squat rack, the Smith machine provides a fixed bar path. This can help reduce the risk of injury and ensure a stable lifting environment.

“The Smith machine helps the athlete feel supported and gives them greater control and stability when performing an exercise,” says Mauro M. Maietta, district fitness and education manager for Crunch Fitness.

In particular, fresh lifters can benefit from starting out on a Smith machine so they can focus on their form while being supported by the machine.

It has been revealed that “Maintaining correct form is important for avoiding injuries and maximizing the effectiveness of your workouts,” says Dr. Christopher Mohr, PhD, RD. “Beginners might benefit from working with a personal trainer initially or taking a beginner class to learn proper techniques.”.

The guided motion and added stability of a Smith machine makes it an ideal training tool for those returning from injury or anyone with mobility problems. It encourages proper form and can be a safer way to increase your strength and joint stability before moving on to free weights.

It has been revealed that maietta recommends starting with lighter weights to get a feel for the range of motion before progressing. “The fixed range of motion is not for everyone, so be sure to speak with your local fitness professional and listen to your body and joints if you feel any discomfort or pain during the planned movements,” he says.

If you prefer to work out alone or don’t have a training partner available, the Smith machine can act as a “spotter” for you. These machines offer an extra layer of safety, as you can easily rack the bar or set the safety spotters to a specific point that will keep you out of harm’s way.

In addition, this advantage allows you to safely follow progressive overload, a proven method for increasing muscle size and strength.

“This continual challenge helps your muscles grow stronger,” states Mohr. “It’s important to start with manageable increments to prevent injury.”.

Recent findings suggest that you won’t find many machines that offer as much versatility as the Smith machine. Want to train legs? You can knock out squat and lunge variations. Want to grow your chest and shoulders? Grab an adjustable weight bench and work on your bench press and overhead press without having to worry about keeping the bar stable. A high-end option like the Force USA G15 gives you the ability to perform cable exercises like cable crossovers, chest flys, and overhead triceps extensions.

“The Smith machine can be seen as the Swiss army knife of the weight room since it allows for several strength training exercises in its fixed vertical path, ranging from squats to overhead pressing movements,” says Maietta.

According to recent reports, what should you consider when choosing a Smith machine? Based on our experience as equipment experts and dedicated lifters, here’s what we recommend:.

It has been revealed that consider the machine’s footprint when determining if it is a good fit for your needs. One benefit of Smith machines is all-in-one trainers are available to consolidate the space needed for multiple workout stations.

Many of the home gym Smith machine options on this list are designed as all-in-one trainers designed to provide multiple workout functions with one convenient machine. The machine can include stations for a power rack, functional trainer, low-row attachment, chin-ups/pull-ups, dips, suspension trainers, and more.

In a recent development, smith machines offer pulley systems with varying weight ratios, including 1:1 and 2:1. A 1:1 ratio means the weight you load is the exact weight you lift. A 2:1 ratio means you lift half of the weight you load. For instance, with a 2:1 ratio, if you load 100 pounds, you lift 50 pounds.

Some Force USA Smith machines, including the G15, allow users to easily switch between 2:1 and 4:1 ratios, which is helpful when people of various skills use the same machine.

It has been revealed that weight capacities vary depending on the functions offered by the machine. The weight capacities on this list start at 300 pounds. Be sure to confirm the machine’s weight capacity can accommodate your needs..

Sources indicate that if you are looking for versatile strength-building home gym equipment to achieve a full-body workout, a Smith machine can help you achieve your goals. Since the 1950s, this game-changing machine has allowed gym-goers to work out safely without a spotter. Today, there is a wide range of consumer options, allowing you to experience the benefits of the Smith machine in the comfort of your own home gym.

Industry observers note that smith machines all perform similar functions, but there are different types of Smith machines available. For instance, some Smith machines provide a vertical path for motion, while other Smith machines provide a slightly angled path. Some Smith machines may be limited to the Smith machine function, while others are designed to be all-in-one machines with multiple stations for different exercises. Smith machines vary based on the manufacturer.

Yes, you can deadlift on a Smith machine, but whether you should depends on your skills and ability.Maietta suggests thinking through the following questions before performing moves on a Smith machine:-How is your range of motion?-Do you have the proper form or mobility to perform these compound moves?If you do not know, Maietta suggests working with a local fitness professional who will be able to help coach you and correct your form if necessary.

In a recent development, yes, you can build muscle with the consistent use of a Smith machine. Smith machines are considered a good strength and muscle training option for beginners or those without a spotter. However, the drawback is motion is limited to a specific vertical (or slightly angled) path. For sports-specific muscle building, some experts prefer free weight exercises.

Yes, you can squat with a Smith machine. Safety features such as hooks and stoppers can help provide extra protection. Again, be mindful of your abilities and consult with a fitness pro if you are unsure of how to do this safely and with proper form.

Hyatt operates on a fixed award chart, ranging from 3,500 points for a Category 1 night all the way up to 45,000 points for a Category 8 night. Unlike programs that use dynamic pricing (where award costs swing with cash demand), Hyatt's chart is static. A Category 4 property costs the same 15,000 points whether it's a Tuesday in February or New Year's Eve.

Recent findings suggest that your free night certificate functions exactly like those 15,000 points — but you earned it through card spending, not through a points balance. This means the certificate has a defined and predictable value: whatever a Category 4 property charges in cash on the night you use it is exactly what you're getting for free.

Your certificate captures that peak-season value without any upcharge.
